items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: Cyrus Chestnut was on piano and a gentleman, Vinnie Johnson on drums... we did a performance

ctx.x: That’s tough in two respects because a lot of times the women’s voices, if they’re doing standards, you’re not doing them in the standard key anymore. You’re doing “Misty” in B flat and stuff like that.

Well another one I think was when I was down with Benny Waters in New York I think it was at the St. Peter’s Church, and we did a performance. Cyrus Chestnut was on piano and a gentleman, Vinnie Johnson on drums. And Benny had called off a tune, a ballad I’d never heard of before. And I think there were about three hundred people at this performance. People were sitting on the floor, I mean it was packed. And all of a sudden Benny calls out this tune, he’s calling it off, and I have no idea, I’ve never heard of…

Did you ever get in those situations where it’s like a jam session and you’re playing one tune for fifteen or twenty minutes and all the horn players finally get their thing done, and then they give it to you?
